messages:
maya: Heads-up — following the postmortem for last night's OOMs. Starting a thread to track owners, timelines, and concrete follow-ups for the KV "shelf reserve" residency growth. Short-term mitigations + long-term root cause work. Please ack and pick owners.

tom: Ack. Can you paste the key symptoms we saw?

maya: OOMs on prod shard group west-2 between 00:13–00:28. Heap profiles show steady KV residency growth (~25MB/min) during low traffic. Eviction counters low, but allocs keep climbing. Suspect ghost refs from lazy-evict path.

anita: I uploaded heap + slab maps and malloc traces: s3://redwood-artifacts/oom/347890/pprof.tar.gz

zack: :eyes: grabbing artifacts. Quick triage plan: (1) enable slab debug on a canary host, (2) add a per-shard soft-limit + alert, (3) validate GC sweep frequency and weird fragmentation patterns.

liam: For immediate mitigation, soft-limit looks fastest. Can we set a conservative threshold to stop growth before full OOM?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-34789 — page sent to oncall.

maya: Action items — short list (please claim):
A1) Soft limit + alert (temporary mitigation) — owner: liam — due: EOD today
A2) Canary slab debug + full heap capture with debug symbols — owner: zack — due: tomorrow AM
A3) Root cause profiling + malloc_trace deep analysis — owner: anita — due: next Wed
A4) Eviction fairness tweak + regression tests (prevent starvation) — owner: tom — due: 2 weeks
A5) Retro + postmortem follow-ups board entry — owner: tom — due: Fri EOD

tom: I'll open a PR for eviction fairness + include unit/integration tests that simulate slow-growth scenarios.

anita: malloc_trace shows frequent retains from ChunkRef::retain called by archived request cache path — hypothesis: coroutine contexts not being cleared on session teardown, leaving dangling refs.

zack: I can reproduce locally with the session-reuse harness. Pushing a patch to explicitly clear coroutine cache on session close. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/12345

maya: For soft-limit numbers: propose soft_limit = 0.8 * peak_mem, escalation to 0.6 * peak when alert fires. liam, can you confirm numbers and cooldown?

liam: Confirmed. Canary thresholds: 75% -> scale to 60% on alert with a 5min cooldown to avoid thrash. I'll add an alert rule and a playbook note.

anita: Running a long-run heap capture overnight on staging with slab-debug enabled. Also added perf counters: kv.active_references and kv.eviction_rate.

zack: Will run canary deploy tomorrow 03:00 UTC. If clean, roll to west-2 by 06:00.

maya: Good. Retro: who will draft the follow-up notes and track the postmortem action board?

tom: I will own the retro write-up and make the GH issue that tracks follow-ups. ETA Fri EOD.

liam: Suggestion: add a weekly automated residency-trend check (7d growth detector) so we catch low-signal drifts before they hit OOM. I can prototype a metric query and alert.

maya: Agree — add as long-term action: automated drift detector (owner: liam) due: 3 weeks.

zack: After mitigation, I'll run a full soak with varied session counts to validate no regressions.

anita: If the malloc_trace hypothesis holds, fix will be to zero the coroutine cache on teardown and add a regression test that asserts no retained refs after N cycles.

maya: Summary closure: liam + zack pair for the deploy/mitigation; anita to confirm root cause; tom to land eviction tests and own retro. I'll update the postmortem with this owner/timeline list and tag SRE for validation.

sre-bot: Update: INC-2026-34789 -> status: mitigated (soft limits applied).

maya: Thanks everyone — please update the GH issue with PR links and any new artifacts. We'll reconvene after staging soak for the final RCA.
